text:
maria: Quick share — ran Deckard-9b on a mixed slice (search+chat+long-summary). Comparing int8 baseline vs a new int6 build. Posting top-level econ + quality notes.
shaun: Top-line numbers please.
maria: TL;DR: int6 saves ~40% token cost vs int8 but shows a small quality hit concentrated in long-form tasks.
maria: Measurements on a 10k-sample eval (stratified):
- latency (p50/p95): int8 = 85ms / 250ms, int6 = 78ms / 320ms
- cost (per 1M tokens): int8 = $15.2, int6 = $9.1
- pairwise winrate (annotator): int6 vs int8 = -3.2% (CI ±0.8%)
- hallucination score (lower is better): int8 = 2.1, int6 = 3.0 (absolute units from annotator rubric)
- downstream: summarization (>256 tok) MRR / ROUGE-like drop ~1.1-6.8% depending on subset
liyah: p95 tail on int6 is pretty bad (320ms). Was this with warmed KV caches and same batch settings?
maria: Yes — both variants warmed with 2k prefix, same continuous batching config. The tail appears to be from occasional kernel fallback on some GPUs (profile shows expensive slow path ~0.4% of tokens).
shaun: Do we have signal split — where exactly is quality regression concentrated?
maria: Short prompts (<128 tok) winrate ~ -1.0%. Long-form (>256 tok) winrate ~ -6.8%. Dialog-turn coherence drops slightly on multi-turn >6 turns.
nina: If cost savings are large for chat but quality hits for docs/summaries, can we do per-route routing to get best of both?
maria: Yes — proposal below. Simple routing rules + fallback to int8 for long summaries and any safety/regression signals. Also add latency-based fallback.

```yaml
routes:
  - match: { intent: summarization }
    model_variant: deckard-9b-int8
  - match: { intent: chat }
    model_variant: deckard-9b-int6
fallback_p95_ms: 500
```

Add rollout as canary 5% then 20% with monitoring on quality metrics (winrate, hallucination) and latency SLOs.
product-sam: From GTN perspective — Docs product needs long-form fidelity. Recommend default summarization route -> int8, enable int6 as a cost-optimized opt-in for chat/autocomplete. Capture a simple metric for customers: quality_delta_on_sample and cost_savings_pct.
ops-bot: Canary deployment kicked off at 4798765450 — 5% chat traffic -> deckard-9b-int6. Monitoring alert on p95 > 600ms.
liyah: One more detail: current int6 build uses per-tensor scales. I ran a quick per-channel qparams experiment and it reduces the long-form delta by ~1.8 points (winrate), but adds ~3% compute overhead vs naive int6. Worth sweeping.
maria: Next actions I propose: 1) run per-channel int6 sweep on 50k heterogeneous sample, 2) simulate unit-econ for 10M tokens/day to project monthly savings, 3) add routing rules + latency fallback to canary. I'll post a scoreboard tomorrow with cost per 1M tokens, projected monthly savings, and winrate by slice.
shaun: If per-channel int6 moves winrate to > -1.5% while keeping >30% cost savings vs int8, I endorse rolling to GA for chat routes with docs pinned to int8.
nina: :thumbsup: Good plan, and please include the exact eval slice definition in the scoreboard (we need reproducibility).
ops-bot: Canary progress update 4798765475 — 5% traffic steady, no infra errors, p95 observed 310ms for int6 on canary nodes.
maria: Noted. Will run the 50k sweep overnight and share numbers in this thread (expected by 4798766480).
